tagline: Down the San Pedro, across the Gila, into the mountains.
intro: North of Mammoth, SR 77 crosses the San Pedro River and keeps to its east bank, past the turn for Aravaipa Canyon, whose name is Apache for laughing waters. At Winkelman the northward-flowing San Pedro runs into the westward-flowing Gila, and the highway crosses the Gila beside the old bridge.

From there it follows the Gila's west bank for seven miles, then leaves the river and works up through mountainous country by Dripping Springs and El Capitan. It was already an old road when the state took it on in 1938, laid down to tie the mining camps to the towns and the railroads.

moments.title: Dudleyville
moments.text: A stage stop on the Globe to Tucson road from the late 1870s, eclipsed in 1904 when the railroad went to Winkelman, a mile north.

moments.title: Winkelman Bridge
moments.text: The highway crosses the Gila beside the old Winkelman Bridge, built in 1916 at a town named for a local cattleman.

moments.title: Christmas
moments.text: Two prospectors staked the claim in the early hours of Christmas Day 1902 and named it for the day. Nobody lives there now, but its post office once drew holiday mail wanting the postmark.
